p14arf and NPM1 form high‐molecular‐weight soluble complexes through an interaction that involves a novel p14arf C‐terminal motif.
p14arf interacts with the N‐terminal domain of NPM1 via a previously uncharacterized motif, which is located in the C‐terminus of p14arf and corresponds to its nucleolar localization signal.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the interaction between p14arf and NPM1, a key event for the control of the p14ARF‐HDM2 axis and the maintenance of genomic stability.
a novel mechanism of p14arf regulation by NPM1, which is likely to be relevant for the pathogenesis of NPM1 mutated leukemia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N‐terminal NPM1 domain interacts with the p14arf C‐terminal region and that this interaction is critical to regulate the p14arf cellular localization and stability.
p14arf‐mediated inhibition of HDM2 activity is a crucial mechanism for the tumor suppression function of p14arf.
NPM1 is a negative regulator of p14arf and, in turn, of its tumor suppressor functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the p14arf C‐terminal region, which we identified as a nucleolar localization signal and as a novel NPM‐interaction motif, represents a new regulatory domain of the protein that is involved in its tumor suppression function.

p14arf and NPM1 interact in solution and this interaction is mediated by the C‐terminal domain of p14arf and the N‐terminal domain of NPM1, thus providing a structural basis for the regulation of p14arf activity by NPM1.

p14arf is a novel NPM substrate and the interaction between the two proteins is mediated by the p14arf C‐terminal region, whose sequence and structure are conserved among different vertebrate species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NPM1 is a key regulator of p14arf activity and its deregulated expression or function may contribute to the development of cancer.
